newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU economy in '97 to show mixed results--survey.
newsitem.headline: EU economy in '97 to show mixed results--survey.

text.p: A slow creep upwards in business confidence, stagnant jobs growth and a small rise in investment plans is expected for the European Union in 1997, EUROCHAMBRES, an association of EU chambers of commerce, said on Tuesday.

In a wide-ranging survey covering 97 economic regions and 12 of the EU's 15 member states, the group found that most entrepreneurs are cautious and "uncertain about the force of the current recovery, or its length".
The business climate was most positive in Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Britain, Ireland and the Netherlands, with strong export growth followed recently by a pickup in domestic demand.
The survey also showed that efforts to meet the preconditions of a single European currency could affect business in both positive and negative ways.

"Budgetary cuts may suppress domestic demand. On the other hand, the resulting better-balanced national budgets may instil faith in the financial markets, thereby lowering interest rates, which is conducive to investments," the survey said.
There was little change expected in labour markets, with notable differences throughout the EU.
France, Britain and Spain showed a slight improvement in firms' expectations for creating jobs, while Germany's outlook remained rather weak.
Meanwhile, the strong growth in employment seen recently in Denmark and Sweden was not expected to be matched this year.
